papers.relied_on: Derivation paper of the C-peptide-containing remission score; row 11 cites it as the source of the score, with no duration comparison.
papers.full_text_shows: Derivation n=63 (48 remission, 15 not), validation n=176 (remission 65.3% at 1 year, bypass only). C-peptide stayed in the multivariate model (P=.006) with age, BMI and duration, so it was independently associated within the derivation cohort, but no model with and without C-peptide and no comparison with duration alone is reported. The paper uses the name Diabetes Surgery Score only; it never says ABCD. Patients with C-peptide above 9 ng/mL were excluded (to exclude type 1).
papers.quote: the predictive power is limited in patients with a lower Diabetes Surgery Score.
papers.key_numbers: Multivariate P=.006 for C-peptide; score 8 vs 4 (remission vs not, P<.05); remission 33% at score 0 to 100% at score 10; +6.7% per point; 1-year follow-up. C-peptide point bands are garbled in the extraction and not recorded.
papers.role_in_work: Derivation and validation source for the score; steelman-run citation.
papers.design: Derivation cohort plus prospective validation cohort, 1-year remission.
papers.population_and_size: Derivation n=63 (gastric bypass, 3-year follow-up), validation n=176 (2008-2010, 5 Asian countries); BMI 21.5-64.9 in validation.
papers.measure_type: C-peptide, presumably fasting (timing not stated in the text read).
papers.assay_or_platform: Not reported in the extracted text.
papers.quality_note: Small derivation sample, short follow-up, Asian bypass cohorts, no comparison with duration alone; table extraction partly garbled. A disclosure line appears to say no conflict of interest (partly read).

papers.relied_on: Row 11 lists DSS-II as a guideline source; no C-peptide recommendation expected.
papers.full_text_shows: Brief communication summarising the DSS-II consensus (Delphi process, voting). It argues that baseline BMI does not predict metabolic-surgery benefit. It does not mention C-peptide or any remission score; it mentions only that fasting plasma insulin predicts cardiovascular events after surgery. Two-column extraction is garbled.
papers.quote: nonanthropometric parameters such as fasting plasma insulin levels predict cardiovascular events after surgery
papers.key_numbers: No C-peptide mention in the text.
papers.design: Short commentary on a consensus conference.
papers.population_and_size: Adults with type 2 diabetes considered for metabolic surgery; no cohort.
papers.measure_type: None for C-peptide; fasting insulin mentioned once as a cardiovascular predictor.
papers.quality_note: Summary of the consensus, not the full guideline.

papers.relied_on: Merged conclusion: duration alone had AUROC 0.84 at 2 years against 0.79-0.88 for five scores and was no worse at 10 years.
papers.full_text_shows: Confirms the abstract figures. The ABCD score (age, BMI, C-peptide, duration) had the lowest 2-year AUROC (0.79) of the five and was not better than duration alone at 2 or 10 years (0.70 vs 0.73). DiaBetter and IMS beat duration alone at 2 years. Calibration was assessed only for DiaRem-family scores (too optimistic). Only 39 gastric bypass patients, so the derivation surgery type was barely represented. No C-peptide-only model was run.
papers.quote: no score had higher predictive capacity than diabetes duration alone
papers.key_numbers: n=363. 2-year AUROC: ABCD 0.79, DiaRem 0.86, Ad-DiaRem 0.85, DiaBetter 0.88, IMS 0.88, duration 0.84. 10-year: ABCD 0.70, DiaRem 0.72, Ad-DiaRem 0.71, DiaBetter 0.74, IMS 0.76, duration 0.73. Gastric bypass subgroup n=39.
papers.role_in_work: Main comparative evidence for D2 and D8 of row 11; steelman-run citation.
papers.design: Post hoc analysis of the prospective, non-randomised Swedish Obese Subjects surgery group.
papers.population_and_size: 363 surgically treated SOS participants with type 2 diabetes at baseline; mostly banding or vertical banded gastroplasty.
papers.measure_type: C-peptide, fasting (overnight fast), as one input of the ABCD score.
papers.assay_or_platform: C-peptide and HbA1c analysed at St Vincent's Healthcare Group, Dublin (ISO 15189 accredited); assay not named in the passages read.
papers.quality_note: Good: prospective, long follow-up; remission by single-time-point glucose or HbA1c. Duality of interest: consulting fees from AstraZeneca and Johnson & Johnson; advisory boards for Novo Nordisk and others.

papers.relied_on: Row 11 lists it as a cohort showing C-peptide associated with remission after gastric bypass.
papers.full_text_shows: Retrospective n=100 plus prospective n=20 (Sao Paulo). Of age, duration, insulin use, HbA1c, C-peptide and basal insulin, only C-peptide above 3 ng/dL [sic; ng/mL elsewhere] was a positive predictor, tested with univariate tests only. Prospective: 9 of 12 remitters and 0 of 6 non-remitters had C-peptide >3 ng/mL (P=0.014). Does not compare with duration or scores.
papers.quote: only a C-peptide level>3 ng/dL was a positive predictor (p=0.004) of late postoperative diabetes remission.
papers.key_numbers: Remission 72% at 3 years (n=100). Prospective 9/12 vs 0/6 with C-peptide >3 ng/mL, P=0.014.
papers.role_in_work: Supporting cohort for C-peptide as a predictor.
papers.design: Retrospective plus small prospective cohort, univariate tests only.
papers.population_and_size: 100 retrospective and 20 prospective patients with severe obesity and type 2 diabetes after Roux-en-Y bypass.
papers.measure_type: C-peptide, preoperative; fasting status not stated.
papers.quality_note: Low: small, no multivariable adjustment, remission definition allows metformin; no conflict statement seen.

papers.relied_on: Row 11 lists it as a cohort in which C-peptide predicted remission.
papers.full_text_shows: 151 patients evaluated at 2 years; complete remission 49.7%. In multivariable logistic regression higher fasting C-peptide was an independent predictor of complete remission (OR 6.09, 95% CI 1.87-18.84) with shorter duration (OR 1.99) and lower BMI (OR 1.16). No comparison with duration-only or score models. Competing interests: none.
papers.quote: shorter duration of DM, lower BMI, and higher C-peptide levels were the independent factors predicting CR.
papers.role_in_work: Extra cohort that retains C-peptide in a multivariable model.
papers.population_and_size: 151 patients with type 2 diabetes and obesity after sleeve gastrectomy (n=68) or bypass (n=83).
papers.assay_or_platform: Not named in the passages read.
papers.quality_note: Moderate-low: wide confidence interval, small; some table C-peptide values look inconsistent between tables and were not checked.

proposals.reason: Full texts confirm observational-accuracy evidence; C081 adds a multivariable result but wide and small; no guideline or randomised evidence. No change.
proposals.quote: shorter duration of DM, lower BMI, and higher C-peptide levels were the independent factors predicting CR.

proposals.reason: C064 confirms the C-peptide score was weakest at 2 years and no better than duration at 10; no paper tests models with and without C-peptide. No change.
proposals.quote: no score had higher predictive capacity than diabetes duration alone

proposals.reason: DSS-II text does not mention C-peptide; the current 2 rests on rule 5 (V20). No change.
proposals.quote: nonanthropometric parameters such as fasting plasma insulin levels predict cardiovascular events after surgery

claim_issues.issue: Identity of the Diabetes Surgery Score and ABCD is unconfirmed. C024 never uses the name ABCD; C064 and C070 describe ABCD with the same four variables. Likely the same, but no text read states it.
Still true for increment over duration. Add a caveat: C024 and C081 keep C-peptide in multivariable models (P=.006; OR 6.09, CI 1.87-18.84) while C070 used univariate tests only.
Confirmed: C070 uses 3 ng/mL (printed as ng/dL), C024 excludes above 9 ng/mL and uses point bands.
Confirmed by C064. Add: ABCD had the lowest 2-year AUROC (0.79) and SOS was mostly non-bypass surgery (bypass subgroup n=39); measure is fasting C-peptide.

notes: No score change proposed (all three proposals null). Path to viability of row 11 (a study showing C-peptide adds to duration, insulin use and BMI) is unchanged; C081 and C024 hint at independence but did not test increment. Current scores taken from ranking.json and V20-V24 (D3 2 per V20 supersedes S1 value 1; D6 differs between V23 (3) and V24 (2)). Text of C024 and C043 came from PDF extraction with garbled tables; assay and the C043 conflict statement were not found. The C024 quote comes from the extraction and should be checked against the file before reuse. Used 13 tool calls.
